(In practice a typical dose is 500 mg given in- travenously with other vitamins every 8 hours, for 2 days if symptoms persist, and followed by 100 mg twice daily orally, or 250 mg daily intravenously until the patient can take oral thia- mine.6,8) The ataxia and acute confusional state may also resolve dramatically although improvement may not be noted for days or months. Even several months after the onset of symptoms, treat- ment with high doses of thiamine has occasionally resulted in recovery.9 The effects of the syndrome on memory are much harder to reverse.
